title: Picard fixed models: geometric comparison restricted to target cycles
statement: Let f:X to S and fi:Xi to S, i in Fin n, be flat proper locally of finite presentation, with ui:Xi to X over S. Assume the structure adjunction unit of f is universally an isomorphism. Let L be invertible, k:W to S an immersion, w in an affine open U of W, s=k(w), and suppose L_s descends from a finite locally free module on Spec kappa(s). Supply trivializations of each ui-pullback coefficient over Xi times S U. Supply a connective strictly perfect source model K of Rf_W L_W, a basis e1 of its degree-one sections of rank m, and connective strictly perfect target models C_i of Rfi_W(ui^*L)_W, with C_i.d(0,1)=0. With p the kernel of evaluation A=Gamma(W,U) to kappa(w), assume all source section differentials vanish after tensoring with kappa(p). Let Z_i be the kernel of the target residue section differential in degree one. There exist alpha:kappa(p) tensor A^m additively equivalent to H^1(X_s,O), derived arrows a_i:Q(K) to Q(C_i), and additive maps beta_i:Z_i to H^1(Xi_s,O). For every i, every chain representative phi of a_i, and every z in the source coordinate tensor, the residue of Gamma(phi^1) composed with e1 inverse sends z into Z_i, and beta_i of this cycle is ui_s pullback of alpha(z). No map from the entire degree-one target term, no projection onto Z_i, and no product gamma is asserted. Geometry and model notions are [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-perfect-complex, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-sc-invertible-module, def-sc-structure-sheaf-cohomology-pullback, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-residue-field, def-amb-finite-locally-free-module, lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction].

proof.text: Apply the descended-fibre coefficient triviality theorem, using the universal structure unit and the supplied finite locally free descent, to obtain tau:L_s isomorphic to O_Xs.

Apply natural geometric comparison on residue cycles modulo boundaries to the given models and tau. Obtain gamma, a_i, beta_i, surjectivity of gamma, its boundary kernel description, and compatibility on cycles.

The source residue differential in degree zero is zero, so the boundary kernel description makes gamma injective. Together with surjectivity it is an additive equivalence. The source outgoing residue differential is also zero, so the full source degree-one residue term is additively equivalent to its cycle kernel. Compose these two equivalences with tensor extension of e1 inverse to define alpha.

Evaluate the chain-map equation in degree one on affine sections and tensor it with kappa(p). LinearMap.baseChange_comp and the zero source outgoing differential show that each residue image of the coordinate tensor is a target cycle. Apply the naturality assertion and the defining equality for alpha to obtain the required equation for every chain representative.
